counterparts_needing_dossiers.name: Phoenician and Cypriot rebels (Tennes of Sidon)

problems: All four dossiers were written and validate; no page failed. Cross-dossier overlap to settle: twenty-seventh-dynasty-of-egypt models the Persian satrapy of Egypt (525-404) as a dynasty under Achaemenid occupation while achaemenid-empire draws Egypt as its own land from 525; one model must be chosen or Egypt is drawn twice.

Cyprus passes to Persia at 545 in the Twenty-sixth Dynasty dossier and at 525 (before the Egyptian campaign) in achaemenid-empire (Cambyses II page); Phoenicia passes at 539 in the Phoenicia dossier but its Achaemenid event rests on a page that says only 'By 525 BC'.

The macedonian-empire dossier records Bactria and Sogdia as gains from the Achaemenid Empire at 329-327, after achaemenid-empire ends in July 330; the Bessus remnant is a split event with a counterpart that has no dossier.

Cliopatria's Neo-Assyrian Empire (to 601), Urartu (to 551), Neo-Babylonian Empire (to 531), Twenty-sixth Dynasty (to 501), Lydia (to 541) and Egyptian satrapy (in the Achaemenid shape to 384) run past their conquests and overlap neighbouring shapes; the Cliopatria Macedonian Empire (218,000 km2 in Greece, 331-327) and Ptolemaic Kingdom (1.22 M km2 of Egypt, Syria and Turkey, 331) rows split Alexander's 333-331 conquests in a way no page supports.

The Cliopatria Median Kingdom shapes are Iran plus Afghanistan and never reach Anatolia; both verdicts correct this against the 'Medes' page. The Achaemenid 550 shape contains the east that Cyrus conquered in 545-540; corrected.

The kingdom-of-bithynia page budget (5) and the cyrenaica budget (2) left both dossiers thin; neither Wikipedia article gives an infobox area. Counterpart slugs without a dossier yet: seleucid-empire, kingdom-of-pontus, paphlagonia, antigonid-macedonia, ptolemaic-kingdom (other me-05 parts or eu groups).
